_purpose: Canonical model routing table for Bag End fan-out. The workflow templates (tools/workflows/*.js) consume this via args. NEVER hand-compose provider/model pairs in a delegation prompt — copy from here. Provider ids must match ~/.dsh/settings.yaml llm-pi-ai.providers (deepseek-official resolves via the harness registry; see flash_team note).

_policy.preflight_note: A single null is not a dead route. Transient failures look identical to structured-output contract failures and to route death; retry N times before condemning a leg, and record every attempt.
_policy.identity_check: each child quotes the model name from its own system prompt 'powered by the <model> model' line; a mismatch is a routing bug, not noise
_policy.leg_priority: owner ruling 2026-09-08 (supersedes 2026-09-07): assign legs by priority — deepseek-flash (V41-Flash) + glm-5.3-flash first (1), qwen3.8-flash second (2), gpt-5.6-luna third (3); fall through to a lower priority only when higher-priority routes are exhausted or unsuitable for the batch

subagent_model_pinning.bound_to: the `subagent` tool's schema, built once at SESSION START. Enabling the setting mid-session, or restarting dsh and resuming an old conversation, leaves the old schema in place. The fix is a NEW CONVERSATION — a restart is not enough. Verified empirically 2026-09-12: the identical call failed with the error below in the resumed session `COS - dsv41-flash` and succeeded in the next new session.
subagent_model_pinning.disabled_error: Error: child model selection is disabled for this tool instance
subagent_model_pinning.verified_2026_09_12: all four flash routes pinned on `subagent`; every child quoted its own identity line verbatim and executed bash + read + glob (deepseek-flash, glm-5.3-flash, qwen3.8-flash, gpt-5.6-luna). `workflow` agent() separately pinned glm-5.3-flash + qwen3.8-flash and used tools — proved by two children writing unique nonce files to disk, confirmed from the COS shell.
subagent_model_pinning.not_available_on: `subagent_fork` — its schema omits provider/model by design, keeping the child's route equal to the parent so the inherited prefix stays eligible for KV-cache reuse. `workflow` agent() accepts provider/model but REJECTS reasoning_effort: effort pinning is subagent-only.
subagent_model_pinning.untested: reasoning_effort pinning — children do not report their effort, so the identity check cannot confirm it. Test per route before relying on it; gpt-5.6-luna is effort-value sensitive ('minimal' 400s).
subagent_model_pinning.steerability: `subagent` and `subagent_fork` children are continuable and answer send_message; `workflow` agent() children are one-shot and CANNOT be steered mid-run — re-dispatch instead.
subagent_model_pinning.retires: the 2026-09-10 note that workflow agent() children cannot use tools (a tool-using child resolved to `null` on dsh 0.1.5-rc.1). Retired 2026-09-12; both parked templates are runnable again.

cos.seat: deepseek-flash (display name DeepSeek-V41-Flash) — OWNER RULING 2026-09-08: V41-Flash supersedes the 2026-09-07 pro-chair ruling and holds the COS seat; deepseek-v4-pro/deepseek-v4-flash retired from this table (legacy ids remain in the harness catalog)
cos.independence: legs are ALWAYS separate instances with self-contained briefs — no shared context with the COS — so a deepseek-flash leg verifies the COS instance independently of its reasoning (owner clarification 2026-09-08). What same-model legs cannot cover is model-level (correlated) error: identical weights share identical blind spots. Safeguard: every batch keeps at least one cross-family leg (glm-5.3-flash, or qwen3.8-flash/gpt-5.6-luna), and the chair model stays excluded from post-hoc pro review
